title: Two animals, one visit
hook: A small observation has a limited reach.

knows: Animals can act and respond to conditions.
doesNotKnow: In one visit, animal A approaches a novel object and animal B stays back. What does that observation alone establish?

misconception: One observed behavior always supports a broad or causal conclusion.
objective: In one visit, animal A approaches a novel object and animal B stays back. What does that observation alone establish?

claims.text: In one visit, animal A approaches a novel object and animal B stays back. What does that observation alone establish? The panels show different actions by two individuals in one stipulated observation. That supports a statement about those actions, not a species-wide rule or a reliable frequency. A larger, representative and repeated study would be needed for broader inference.
claims.source: Stipulated toy observations; not observed animal data. Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, Behavioral Biology, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-7-behavioral-biology

claims.text: The panels show a stipulated illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
One bird uses a tool during one observed visit. What can that visit alone establish? One observation establishes the observed event, not a universal frequency.
